text: Why, LORD, do you stand far off? Why do you hide yourself in times of trouble?
In his arrogance the wicked man hunts down the poor; let them be caught in the schemes they devise.
The wicked man boasts of the cravings of his heart; he blesses the greedy and spurns the LORD.
In his pride the wicked man does not seek God; God is nowhere in all his thoughts.

versions.text: In his pride the wicked will not seek him; in all his thoughts there is no room for God.
versions.explanation: The pronoun "him" has no antecedent yet (God is named only in the following clause), which is confusing when read aloud. Also the present tense keeps the pattern of the surrounding description (v. 3, 5) rather than shifting to future.

text: His ways prosper at every turn; your judgments are far above him, out of his sight; he sneers at all his enemies.
He says in his heart, "I will never be shaken; no harm will touch me, from generation to generation."
His mouth is filled with cursing, deceit, and oppression; under his tongue are malice and trouble.
He lies in wait near the villages; from hiding he murders the innocent, watching in secret for the helpless.
He lurks in his hiding place like a lion in the thicket; he lies in wait to seize the poor, and seizes them, dragging them off in his net.
His victim is crushed and sinks down; the helpless fall beneath his strength.
He says in his heart, "God has forgotten; he has hidden his face and will never see."

versions.text: He says in his heart, "God has forgotten; he has hidden his face and will never see it."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has no object; adding "it" narrows the sense unnecessarily. The absolute "will never see" matches the original and reads cleanly aloud.

text: Rise up, LORD! Lift up your hand, O God. Do not forget the afflicted.
Why does the wicked man revile God and say in his heart, "He will not call me to account"?
But you do see; you take note of trouble and grief, to take it into your hand. The victim commits himself to you; you are the helper of the fatherless.
Break the arm of the wicked and the evildoer; call him to account for his wickedness, until none is found.
The LORD is King forever and ever; the nations will perish from his land.
You hear the longing of the afflicted, LORD; you strengthen their heart and incline your ear,
to bring justice to the fatherless and the oppressed, so that mere mortals of the earth may strike terror no more.

versions.text: to bring justice to the fatherless and the oppressed, so that mere mortals of the earth may terrify no more.
versions.explanation: "May terrify no more" leaves the verb objectless and sounds clipped when read aloud; "strike terror no more" conveys the Hebrew verb naturally and closes the psalm with better rhythm.
